speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens right before you become unresponsive, and do you recall any specific sensations or triggers?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of head trauma or prior seizures, and does your family have any history of epilepsy or neurological disorders? I would also like to know if these episodes occur more frequently during sleep or upon waking.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the episodes happen exclusively during sleep, and does he exhibit automatisms like lip-smacking or repetitive hand movements? I would like to request an EEG to evaluate for temporal lobe epilepsy. REQUEST TEST: EEG
